title: Can Your Margins Fit a Chicken?

 Can Your Margins Fit a Chicken?
Hi Sara,
Apparently, if you're pruning a peach tree correctly, you should be able to throw a chicken through it.
That's what my father-in-law says anyway…and he is a farmer with a peach orchard, so I’m not going to argue.
Everything can be brought back to accounting firms if you try, and the peach tree made me think about accounting firm margins.
When you’re buying a firm, everyone talks about the profit, but not everyone agrees on what that actually means.
Some buyers use SDE (Seller’s Discretionary Earnings), others throw around EBITDA, and both can be right; it just depends on the type of buyer you are.
Here’s the cheat sheet:
SDE is what matters when you’re going to run the firm yourself. It includes all the ways the seller was paying themselves: salary, car, retirement, maybe even “employing” their teenage son.

EBITDA is what you look at when you’re not running it yourself. You’ll have to hire someone to do the work, so you'll have to back out all those perks and look at what’s left.

But here’s the catch: replacing a good owner-operator isn't easy. They’re usually doing the work of two people, and they know the business inside and out. 
So if you're planning to go full absentee owner, be ready to build a team, not just hire a body.
And if you're buying a firm with multiple partners and stepping in as a solo owner? That's when we start doing a little math magic to normalize things. One-part SDE, one-part EBITDA, all parts “it depends.”
